newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends down on bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends down on bearish sentiment.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
May (3rd pos) 1,236 rgt/tonne Mar (south) 1,282.50*
Open/Hi/Low 1,249/1,250/1,235 Prev close 1,302.50
Prev settlement 1,255 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - The market reversed Tuesday's trend and closed weaker on sellers' squeeze in March futures, bearish USDA report and fears of an increase in local stocks. Trading was volatile with double-digit losses posted at close. May futures traded below 1,250 and the near-term bearish trend is intact.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Also fell, with weak fundamentals affecting sentiment. Millers and refiners were seen selling.
The bearishness in the spot futures position spilled over to other futures months which also posted double-digit losses.
Benchmark, third month May futures saw more long liquidation and finished the day 19 ringgit lower at 1,236 ringgit ($499.39) a tonne after opening at 1,249.

"Technically, the market is expected to be bearish. Soyoil has gone up so much in recent days but didn't come down a lot after the bearish USDA crop report yesterday," a trader said. "Palm oil may come down a bit more."
USDA on Tuesday surprised the market by leaving the 1996-97 soybean stocks estimate at 140 million bushels. Traders had expected a cut in the carryout tally of 10-15 million bushels.
"Fundamentally, there is a lot of speculations on the stocks/output data in the market. We have to wait for some fresh crop data this weekend to gauge the market direction," another trader said.
Private forecaster, Ivan Wong will release his final February crop estimates on Friday ahead of the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's data on Saturday.
"We feel that crop estimates in coming months will be bearish because of the better weather conditions as well as the seasonal low production period being over," a trader said.
Poorer than expected exports coupled with better production prompted players to liquidate their long liquidation, they said.
Some traders said millers were undersold and also anxious to sell before prices became less attractive.

Among physicals, Mar (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,282.50 ringgit against bids of 1,275 after trading from 1,282.50 to 1,277.50. Mar (central) saw offers at 1,265 against bids of 1,257.50 with earlier trades done at 1,265 and 1260.
Apr (south) was offered at 1,280 with bids at 1,270, with early transactions from 1,277.50 to 1,272.50.
Apr (central) saw offers at 1,265 with bids at 1,257.50.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $550 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Apr at $542.50 and May/June at $537.50. Mar was traded at $542.50.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $582.50, Apr at $575 and May/Jun at $570. Apr was dealt at $575 and $576.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $455 and Mar/Apr palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $310.
